newsitem.title: INDIA: India ruling alliance fears crisis talks may fail.
newsitem.headline: India ruling alliance fears crisis talks may fail.

text.p: India's ruling coalition said on Wednesday that make-or-break talks with the Congress party to save Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda's ten-month-old government may not succeed.

"My prognosis is I don't think the talks will succeed, not in the second round, not in the third round," a senior alliance official told reporters after leaders adjourned for the night after a first round of formal talks.
"The 2 1/2-hour-long discussion today was mainly over the Congress delegates' demand for the coronation of Mr. Sitaram Kesri (Congress president) as prime minister," the official said.
"The United Front delegates summarily rejected the suggestion," the official said. "But both sides have agreed to resume their discussions tomorrow."

The coalition's delegates were later locked in talks with Deve Gowda, apparently working out a strategy for Friday's vote of confidence the prime minister faces in parliament, United Front officials said.
United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy said the talks were held in a cordial atmosphere but gave not details.
